best_for: People who copy, sync or back up files between their Windows PC and cloud storage from the command line or scheduled scripts, often across several providers.
description:
Rclone is a command-line program for managing files on cloud storage, written in Go and first inspired by rsync. The site carries Nick Craig-Wood's copyright from 2014 on, and a large user community answers questions in its forum. Other developers build backup tools and GUIs on top of it.

It checks MD5 and SHA1 hashes and keeps file timestamps, and a transfer cut off by a weak connection or a quota can pick up from the last good file. When moving data between two providers, it copies on the server side where it can, so the files do not pass through your PC. Bisync keeps two folders in step both ways, and the ncdu command shows what is using space in a cloud account.

points.title: One tool for 70+ services
points.text: Rclone talks to over 70 storage services, from big clouds to S3-style object stores, with commands such as sync, copy, move, check, mount and serve. Learn one tool instead of one app per provider.

points.title: Command line first
points.text: You set it up by running `rclone config` in a command window. There is a web GUI, but the project calls it experimental.

points.title: Encrypt before upload
points.text: The crypt backend encrypts files before they reach the provider, so the cloud only stores scrambled data.

points.title: Mounting needs WinFsp
points.text: To show a remote as a drive letter, install the free WinFsp utility first. A drive mounted from an admin prompt is invisible to other accounts.

points.title: No installer
points.text: The Windows download is a zip with a single rclone.exe you place anywhere; `rclone selfupdate` keeps it current. This site lists x86, x64 and Arm64 zips and keeps 45 Windows versions.

points.title: Free under MIT
points.text: Rclone is open source under the MIT license.

points.title: Mac and Linux elsewhere
points.text: This site lists Windows only. The project offers its own downloads for other systems and is in the Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora repositories. The Homebrew build does not support mount.
